open_questions: Follow-up radial velocity to measure stellar-mass companion (astrometric RUWE 5.044)
dossier.public_summary: A 3-day 18580 ppm dip around a very small M dwarf is flat-bottomed and repeats but is much longer than expected for this star and the star shows Gaia astrometric wobble and excess noise. Only three weak transits are seen. This is best explained as an eclipse of a stellar companion on the target, not a planet.

reasons.why: Gaia RUWE 5.044 is highly elevated; excess_noise_sig 251.4 and ipd_multi_peak 8 indicate astrometric perturbation and multiple peaks, not typical for a single planet host.

Transit duration 3 h is much longer than central 2.157 h (ratio 1.391) for a 0.3515 Rsun M dwarf; fit density strongly inconsistent with stellar density, indicating stellar-radius not as expected — stellar-radius tool shows duration_ratio 1.39 (TIC) and 1.34 (FLAME). Short duration and flat bottom alone are expected for both planets and small-star eclipses.
ML planet_rank 0.05 is in the lowest decile; few known planets score this low, consistent with binary/blend population and the above astrometric and density mismatches.

Medium SNR 10.52 with only 3 transits and top-3 share 0.992 means signal is not well sampled; no secondary (snr 1.403 depth 1488 ppm), no odd/even diff (diff_sigma 1.133), no plausible neighbour within 1px (plausible_within_1px 0) and flat shape (v_sigma -2.455) do not positively favour a planet when density/astrometry disagree.
